summary: Embedding segment-boundary trim causing ID offsets and partial rerank suppression
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that rerank responses intermittently omit expected top candidates after a bulk embed backfill. Symptoms include missing candidate IDs, a persistent -1 offset between embed IDs and metadata IDs, and an increase in rerank latency when the service falls back to a CPU-based verification path.

Impact:
- AtlasSearch results show 15-40% missing top-k items for certain queries after nightly backfill.
- Production traffic (dedicated cluster) experiences elevated tail latency on rerank routes when mismatch detection triggers extra verification work.
- Business impact: user-facing search degradation and customer escalations.

Environment:
- Dedicated account in prod us-west-2 running embed-ingest v0.9.3 and serving-runtime v2.4.1.
- Reranker configured to accept batched embedding uploads and run nearest-neighbor on 1M doc index.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run nightly backfill job uploading embeddings in 10k batches with the embed-upload endpoint (multipart/protobuf).
2) Observe backfill logs that report 200 for ingest but rerank queries afterwards return fewer candidates than expected.
3) Run diagnostic call to /v1/rerank with known query id; compare returned candidate ids to expected metadata list.
4) Re-run same batch but with smaller batch_size=512; issue does not reproduce consistently.

Expected behavior:
- Rerank should return top-k consistent with stored embeddings and metadata.
- No id offsets or missing candidates after successful ingest responses.

Actual behavior:
- Rerank returns N-3 (or variable) candidates; missing ids cluster around segment boundaries (every ~4096 embeddings).
- Temporary increase in rerank latency (~200-800ms) while the verification fallback runs.

Relevant logs / error snippets provided by customer:
- embed-ingest logs show repeated "decoded payload length mismatch" warnings immediately after the nightly backfill windows.
- Reranker audit log: "candidate_id_lookup failed for id=1024003 -> offset -1" (multiple occurrences).
- No 5xx errors returned to the customer; API returned 200 but with missing results array entries.

Additional notes:
- Customer attached sanitized sample batch and an MD5 of pre/post-ingest metadata mapping.
- This appears specific to large batched uploads and to the combination of embed-ingest v0.9.3 + packer config used by AtlasSearch.
- Customer is on a Dedicated cluster and has an active support SLA.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial ticket created with customer-provided artifacts. Escalated to on-call infra.
2026-03-11 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Acknowledged. Requesting sanitized sample batch and exact backfill job config (batch_size, chunk delimiter, multipart flags).

2026-03-12 - AtlasSearch (Customer): Provided sample payloads and confirmed issue reduces when batch_size <= 512. Noted that they use an internal packer that emits a zero-byte delimiter between segments.

2026-03-12 - Luis Ortega (SRE): Reproduced locally against a mirror using embed-ingest v0.9.3. Observed delimiter trim at segment boundary when compressor ran; this produced a 1-byte shift in proto decoding for the first item of the following segment.

2026-03-13 - Elena Park (Servicing Eng): Pushed temporary guard in local build to reject payloads missing expected delimiter and logged detailed offsets. Verified reranker returns consistent top-k when guard inserted.
2026-03-13 - Maya Chen (Support): Informed customer of temporary mitigation and request permission to schedule a short rollback window to v0.9.2. Customer approved.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
1) Reproducer created using customer packer + embed-ingest v0.9.3. Failure occurs when compressor strip/trims trailing zero byte at segment boundary during chunked upload.
2) Protobuf decoder expects fixed delimiter bytes between segments; trimming leads to byte-shift in subsequent message parsing which manifests as an ID offset (-1) at the boundary.
3) Reranker has a defensive verification path that detects id-metadata mismatches and triggers a CPU-based rescan/verification; this explains the latency spike but not the silent omission.
4) Root cause: a change in embed-ingest v0.9.3 that added an aggressive payload size optimization which erroneously removed zero-byte delimiters from multi-segment uploads packed by certain packers.
5) Related PR discovered: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-ingest/pull/972 (optimizations to payload trimming).
6) Reproduction notes: flakiness correlated with upstream packer behavior and batch alignment at 4096-boundary. Smaller batches avoid alignment and therefore avoid the trim case.
7) Additional cross-check: no evidence of index corruption; the issue is at ingest-time decoding and mapping between embedding buffer indices and metadata ids.

Next steps performed:
- Built hotfix branch (embed-ingest@hotfix/restore-delimiter-guard) that reinstates strict delimiter checks and rejects suspect payloads with 422 and clear diagnostic.
- Coordinated rollback plan to revert embed-ingest to v0.9.2 on AtlasSearch dedicated cluster during a 10-minute maintenance window.
- Prepared a reingest/backfill plan to replay any rejected batches and to run an id-consistency check script before re-enabling traffic.
- Added unit tests for multi-segment packing and a fuzz-test harness for common packers used by customers.
resolution:
In-progress remediation and temporary mitigation applied:
- On 2026-03-13 at 03:00 UTC we rolled embed-ingest back to v0.9.2 on the AtlasSearch dedicated cluster. Preliminary checks show rerank candidate counts returned to expected levels for sample queries.
- Hotfix branch added additional validation to detect missing delimiters and fail-fast with 422, preventing silent id offsets. Hotfix PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embed-ingest/pull/984.
- Backfill replay plan: AtlasSearch to re-run nightly backfill for affected windows after we mark those batches as rejected and provide the sanitized artifacts. Support to validate with id-consistency script pre-cutover.
- Follow-ups: mandatory unit tests for delimiter-preserving compressors in CI, runbook update to flag embed-ingest version changes to customers with large-batch workflows, and a postmortem scheduled (owner: Elena Park) to document root cause and prevention steps.

Customer communication: customer notified of rollback and reingest plan; will validate and confirm by 2026-03-15. Ticket remains open until reingest completes and customer confirms full resolution.
